newsitem.title: USA: U.S. forces start build-up in Bosnia for elections.
newsitem.headline: U.S. forces start build-up in Bosnia for elections.

text.p: U.S. forces began a redeployment in Bosnia on Friday that will boost the number of American troops there by up to 50 percent during next month's municipal elections, a Pentagon spokesman said.

The build-up, part of a regular rotation of forces, means the U.S. contingent with the international peacekeeping force will grow to between 11,000 and 12,000 for several weeks to help ensure security during the mid-September elections.
The United States has just under 8,000 troops in the Balkan state now.

Army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Steve Campbell said an advance party from the Second Armored Cavalry Regiment, now at a staging base at Tazar, Hungary went to Tuzla in Bosnia to prepare for the arrival of troops starting next week.
The troops they will replace, from the 3rd Brigade of the 1st Infantry Division, will not leave Bosnia until about two weeks after the elections.
Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters on Thursday the temporary build-up was "to provide some additional presence during the elections..."

He played down the significance of the extra deployment. "We did this before with the national elections (in Bosnia). We had exactly the same type of arrangement. It's temporary. We've been clear and public about this for months," he said.

The U.S. troops are part of a peacekeeping force of more than 30,000 sent to help implement the 1995 Dayton peace accords that ended more than three years of war. The force is due to leave by June 30 next year.
